verdict_reason: 12 tiles found. 11 of the 12, from two independent photographers, are one open-air museum yard. 3506693107 is the decisive frame: the octagonal brick Hanoi Flag Tower (Cot Co) on its stepped fortress base, photographed over a UH-1 helicopter carrying a US white-star roundel, a camouflaged tracked vehicle and a field gun - that combination of the Flag Tower with captured aircraft and armour in the foreground exists only in the courtyard of the Vietnam Military History Museum. The other ten frames (both photographers) are the museum's aircraft-wreckage monument, the tall welded heap of crashed US airframe sections, a jet compressor rotor, a propeller and radial engine, and rows of bomb and missile casings; 4229365779 shows the monument wide, with its black-and-white photograph panel at its foot and the museum's yellow-walled, red-tiled ranges behind it. Only the twelfth frame, a wall of Heroic Mother portraits, cannot be tied to this yard. The pin is on its real subject.

photos.evidence: A pink-painted museum wall hung in a grid with wood-framed colour portraits of very old Vietnamese women, most wearing a gold star-and-wreath medal (the 'Ba me Viet Nam anh hung' Heroic Mother decoration), each with a small screwed-on bilingual caption plate. Enlarging a plate gives only 'Ba Nguyen Thi ...' and 'Hero Mother ...' - unreadable. Such portrait walls exist in more than one Hanoi museum (military history and the Women's Museum among them), so I cannot pick one from the pixels.

The Hanoi Flag Tower: tall octagonal brick shaft with small fan-shaped windows and a glazed octagonal lantern top, standing on a stepped brick fortress base with an arched gateway. In front of it, on the museum apron, a UH-1 helicopter with a white US star-and-bar roundel, a camouflaged tracked APC at right and the breech and wheel of a large field gun at left.

The aircraft-wreckage monument seen against the sky: a welded heap of torn aluminium airframe panels and spars with a tail fin and a crumpled tailplane rising as a spire at the top, mounted on a plinth in a paved yard.

Detail of the same wreckage heap: buckled pale-green and bare-metal fuselage skin panels, a red-and-white striped marking on one section, riveted frames and a torn intake lip, with a green vehicle and the museum's yellow rendered wall visible behind at left.
The wreckage heap with a visitor in a bush hat standing at its base for scale; torn wing and fin sections, a red-painted plinth edge, and trees plus a red-roofed building behind.
Low-angle detail of the monument's summit: a large pale conical nose/radome section wedged among blackened and torn airframe panels, cables and a cylinder, against a white sky.

Museum outdoor store yard: rows of rusting bomb and rocket casings and finned aerial bombs stood on end and laid on cradles, a wire-wrapped mine or float in the foreground, a green artillery piece at left, and a small cream utility building with an orange number plate '58' beside a mounted gun.

The aircraft-wreckage monument photographed wide, with visitors for scale: the full welded pile of crashed airframe sections with a tail fin spire, a framed black-and-white photograph panel standing at its foot on the plinth, and behind it the museum's ranges - yellow rendered single-storey buildings with red-tiled roofs and air-conditioning units.
The same monument from the other side: pale conical nose section at the top over torn fins and panels, hydraulic struts and a wheel bay visible low down, paved yard and trees behind.

The monument's flank with a large jet-engine compressor rotor (visible blade ring and hub) and a corrugated fuselage barrel lying on the ground in front of it, trees and a red-and-yellow banner behind.

Close-up of wreckage panels in the pile: a curved skin panel carrying a partly destroyed painted insignia decal, a crushed engine cowling and a ribbed duct section, all in the same weathered grey-green as the confirmed monument frames.

A three-blade propeller on a radial piston engine, complete with cylinders and accessory plumbing, standing on the paving directly in front of the wreckage pile, with the framed black-and-white photograph panel of 4229365779 immediately behind it.
